gesd_fraction_constraint.status: MECHANISM from the tool's documented parameter, NOT measured
gesd_fraction_constraint.claim: `rej g 0.3 0.05` — the 0.3 is GESD's MAXIMUM OUTLIER FRACTION (TOOLS.md: 'fraction+significance, NOT sigmas'). A transient dwelling more than 30% of a group therefore exceeds what GESD is configured to consider rejecting at all, independently of how obvious the trail is.
gesd_fraction_constraint.consequence: the derived group size currently targets only the GESD BAND (>50). It does NOT consult the transient inventory, so it satisfies this constraint on this session by 11% and by luck. The audit that would constrain it is exactly the step the chain does not run (README-vs-chain contradiction), so the coupling is functional, not just documentary.
gesd_fraction_constraint.test_that_settles_it: the set-03 arms below: a per-track residual at 27% dwell is the first real probe of whether the fraction cap bites in practice

stations.pattern: groups IMPROVES the along-drift extremes (along+1300 FWHM 3.07->2.95, roundness 0.830->0.864 — the control's WORST station) and slightly degrades perpendicular/centre (perp+1300 2.83->2.92, centre 2.64->2.68). linear_gradient.correction: the first run of this compared ABSOLUTE regional levels and read 61% in R — WRONG INSTRUMENT. The arms differ by a near-uniform additive pedestal (R -48.4, G -44.7, B -43.3 ADU, varying only 0.1-0.4 ADU across the five regions) because the groups compose output-normalises sub-stacks that were themselves output-normalised. Absolute levels are not comparable across that.

gradient_adu_maxmin.note: identical within Siril's 0.1 ADU print precision

survivorship_ruled_out: star counts fall ~2-4% at BOTH along and perp stations, but FWHM moves in OPPOSITE directions (along+1300 -0.12, perp+1300 +0.09). Survivorship bias pushes both the same way, so it does not explain the shape change.
leading_mechanism_NOT_ATTRIBUTED: single-pass registers all 500 frames to ONE reference across ~1150 px of drift, so residual distortion error is largest at the drift extremes; groups registers within ~230 px windows and then composes 5 near-identical sub-stacks. Shorter baselines -> smaller residual. This explains the along-drift improvement and the halved off-axis term. It is a MECHANISM consistent with the data, NOT a discriminating test, and the rejection-denominator term has not been excluded by measurement.
third_arm_specified: DOSE-RESPONSE on group size rather than an attempt to hold rejection fixed: rebuild set-01 at --group=250 (2 groups, ~580 px baseline). If the improvement is registration-baseline it should land BETWEEN single-pass and group=100, monotonically. The rejection denominator moves the other way across that series (250 rejects more like 500 than 100 does), so a monotonic shape trend separates them.
consequence_for_the_route: groups is NOT merely cheap — on this data it measures BETTER on the term the undistort route exists to control. That inverts the trade the route choice was framed on: composability was the reason to switch, and frame uniformity may be a second one. Do NOT generalise from one set.
